reviews.metric_limit: Image suite exposes no task queue P95 or mean execution concurrency; compare wall, CPU, RSS and API probes separately

guard_investigation.sentry: Mean execution concurrency fell with shorter task service time, while wall remained flat and queue P95 fell 62.3%; lower occupancy alone is not reduced scheduler capacity. All three complete pairs are retained.
guard_investigation.paperless_ngx: Queue P95 rose 19.0% (2.44s to 2.91s), with 18.1% longer mean task duration; Celery task duration rose 30.5% and queue P95 rose 30.2%. Wall changed only 0.4%. SQLite ownership SQL sequence is identical to the eager baseline in the bounded core audit. This is an investigated cross-host variability signal, not same-runner causal proof.
guard_investigation.superset: Wall +2.0%, queue P95 -2.6%, mean execution concurrency +2.6%.
guard_investigation.saleor: Wall -12.9%, queue P95 -18.7%, mean execution concurrency +7.7%.
guard_investigation.imagededup: Wall change -0.3%, +2.0%, -3.4% across build, comparison, mixed; task queue P95 and mean execution concurrency are not exposed.
guard_investigation.posthog: All three independently recomputed peaks pass: 29, 34, 24. Cross-host wall rose 64.4% while Celery wall rose 62.7%; actual API rate fell 40.0% for DBWorker and 38.5% for Celery. Mean execution concurrency fell 20.1% versus 14.0% for Celery. Same-runner eager-baseline/candidate comparison remains required; lower actual load is not sufficient proof of optimization.
